generation.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit this exact back-view creature illustration. Preserve the soft neutral-gray fur style, huge sideways shaggy ears, slender frame, hands on hips, asymmetric planted stance, orthographic back camera, pure white background and full-body framing. Keep exactly three furry tail plumes extending toward viewer LEFT.
Two specific corrections:
1. Rebuild the tail JUNCTION as one coherent branching anatomy. The shared root is still on the CENTERLINE at the BASE OF THE SPINE. From it, a short, broad, furry common trunk extends slightly rearward and left. All THREE plume stems visibly flow into this same substantial common trunk through ONE clearly readable three-way fork close to the body. The upper stem sweeps upward-left, the middle stem left, the lower stem downward-left. Each stem thickens smoothly into the shared trunk at the fork, with broad blended branch crotches, like tree branches merging into one trunk, but entirely made of soft furry creature anatomy, not wood. Make the proximal stems lie in a shallow fan so NONE crosses in front of another's attachment. The white gaps between the three plumes start farther out, beyond the solid shared junction. Traceable continuous volume from every plume to the root. Do not leave two disconnected-looking plumes emerging from empty space behind a dominant foreground tail. Do not add a fourth stem, braided tails, separate hip roots, rings, collars, or any new anatomy.
2. Tone down the buttock form: make the rear pelvis flatter and less rounded, reduce cheek bulges and the deep central cleft, remove pronounced buttock highlights, soften the hourglass waist-to-hip transition. Use a modest simple fur-covered pelvic volume blending into the upper legs. Keep the same pose; no clothing or props needed.
The main focus of this edit is the clean three-way connection and understated rear anatomy. Match the existing character everywhere else. No text, arrows, diagram labels, ground, cast shadows or additional views.

userDirection.quote: Think through it a little bit more. Your design is showing one base, but then there's two pieces that sort of branch out from mid-air behind the tail. It needs to have the three pieces of the tail form together more cleanly, like the base of a tree trunk does with its branches, rather than just having two more tails spawn out of the one tail that connects to the body. I also want you to tone down the butt form a tad because it's a little too sexual

inspection.notes: Junction widened but individual stem connections remain ambiguous; rear shaping changes too slight. Superseded by run-0007.
